concept: Textarea is the same recessed window as Input, made taller so a person can write several lines. It keeps the label printed above on the inset line and takes the inverse light, so a long note and a short value read as the same kind of part.
family_difference: Textarea grows to several lines, wraps its text, and offers vertical resize inside its column instead of a single fixed-height row.

default_to_avoid.pattern: browser textarea: a bordered box with a diagonal grab handle that can be dragged wider than its column
default_to_avoid.why_not: The corner handle breaks the full-width column and draws a second, unrelated frame; the well already gives the part its edge.

references.source: system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the entry window is a recess in the body

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The well is surface.sunken with elevation.well, the same as Input, so a note field reads as cut into the body.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the inset line above the part
derivation.form: The label, well and messages stack in one column, and the well keeps the full inline size of that column.

derivation.consequence: every part that takes the keyboard shows the same ring
derivation.form: The well draws the focus ring when the text area holds focus, and resize is vertical only so it can never leave its column.

variants.reason: Textarea follows Input, which was derived in its own round with three lab candidates; only the height and the resize rule differ, so no new candidates were rendered.

root.why: The field stacks its label, well and message in one column so the label sits on the inset line above the well.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the printing beside every other part of the unit.

well.why: The recess takes the inverse light, shade on its top-left inner edge, so the person sees where text goes.

field.why: Typed text is primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks.

count.why: The count is printed under the well in secondary ink with tabular figures, like a reading that changes as you type.

hint.why: The hint is secondary ink in the caption size under the well.

error.why: The error is critical red with a glyph and words, never orange and never colour alone.

glyph.why: A printed mark beside the words means invalid is never told by colour alone, for people who cannot see the red.

focus-within.why: The well shows the same dark ring as every part when its text area holds the keyboard focus.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid well draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below names the problem.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled field loses its recess shadow and fades to half, so it reads as not taking input right now.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well keeps a real border and the focus ring uses the system highlight colour.
